blocks.text: Hello Barbara,

To add to Heather's message yesterday: the search is finished and screening has started. The search covered issued patents and published applications directed at the products {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} identified for clearance.

Screening runs in stages. Titles and abstracts come first, to set aside documents about unrelated technology. The independent claims of what remains are then read against your product description. Anything still in question gets a full reading of its claims and specification. What survives that last stage becomes the short list we chart. When the list is ready, we will propose a working session to take you through it before any charting starts.

The claim reading is done against the product description your team sent at the start of the matter. If any feature has changed since then, please send the current drawings or specification sheets now, so that each reading is done once and against the right design.
Nothing found so far is a conclusion about risk. Any view on a particular patent will come from Heather, in writing, after the claim review is complete.
Thanks
Minutes of Working Session
Freedom-to-Operate Analysis for {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}}. Held by video conference. Recorded by Heather Munoz.
Attendees

items: Barbara Blair, Director of Operations, {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}}
Heather Munoz, Partner
Richard Henderson, Patent Agent
Kelly Snyder, Associate

blocks.text: Outcome
Screening is complete. The meeting agreed the short list of third-party patents that will go to full claim review, and the order in which they will be reviewed. No change to scope was requested.
Discussion
1. Screening results. Richard Henderson reported that most search results were set aside at the abstract or independent-claim stage. Those that remain are grouped by patent family on the short list.

Barbara Blair asked how a patent earns a place on the list. Richard Henderson explained that it stays on if any claim could be read on a feature of the product as described. A place on the list says nothing yet about risk.

2. Product description. Barbara Blair confirmed that the description used for screening matches the current design. She will tell us of any change to a short-listed feature while the claim review is open.

3. Pending applications. Kelly Snyder explained that a published application cannot be cleared the way an issued patent can, because its claims may still change before grant. Each pending application of interest will go on a watch list, with status checks entered on the docket.

4. File histories. Kelly Snyder will obtain the prosecution record for every short-listed patent. Amendments and arguments made to the examiner can narrow how a claim is read, and the charts must reflect them.

5. Form of the opinion. Barbara Blair asked whether the result could be a plain yes or no for each patent. Heather Munoz explained that the memorandum will give a view on each patent with the reasoning behind it, and that each view will be qualified.
The memorandum will be marked privileged. Heather Munoz asked that its circulation within {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} be limited to the people who will act on it.
6. Order of review. Richard Henderson proposed charting first the families whose claims track the product most closely. Barbara Blair agreed. Families near the end of their term will be charted last.

7. Time and cost. Kelly Snyder noted that the file histories of the older families are long, and that reading them is the main variable in the time estimate. She will report if that begins to press on the budget.
Action Items

rows: Circulate the short list, with a note on each patent family
Obtain the file history for every short-listed patent
Set up the watch list of pending applications and enter docket status checks
Report any design change that affects a short-listed feature
Begin claim charts, starting with the families ranked first
Review the first claim charts before they go to the client

blocks.text: Updates between sessions will go to Barbara Blair on the existing email thread for the matter. The next session will be set once the first group of claim charts has been reviewed.
Status Report: Freedom-to-Operate Analysis
Privileged and Confidential: Attorney-Client Communication
Prepared for {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} by Richard Henderson, Patent Agent. Responsible partner: Heather Munoz.
1. Where the Analysis Stands
The analysis is at its midpoint, on schedule, and within budget. Screening is finished. Claim charts for the first group of short-listed patents are drafted and are with Heather Munoz for review.
No conclusion has been reached on any patent. Conclusions belong in the final memorandum, after partner review. Nothing in this report should be read as one.
2. Work Completed
The following items are complete as of this report.

items: Search of issued patents and published applications directed at the products identified for clearance.
Screening of the search results in stages, ending in a short list grouped by patent family. The short list was reviewed and agreed at the working session with your team.
File histories obtained for every short-listed patent. Kelly Snyder has read each one for amendments and arguments that narrow how the claims can be read.
A watch list of pending applications, each entered on the firm's docket for regular status checks.

Claim charts for the first group of short-listed patents. Each chart sets every element of the independent claims beside the corresponding feature of the product, or records that the product has no such feature.

blocks.text: How the Charts Are Built

Each independent claim is charted on its own, because the independent claims of one patent can differ in scope. A dependent claim is charted only where the claim it rests on appears to read on the product. Every chart cites the column and line of the specification it relies on, and the file history where an amendment or argument limits a term.
3. Work for the Coming Period
The order below follows the ranking agreed at the working session. The name after each item is the person responsible for it.

items: Claim charts for the remaining short-listed patents. Richard Henderson.

Review of prior art for any patent where every element of a claim appears to be present in the product. The purpose is to see whether a validity position is available. Richard Henderson, with Kelly Snyder.

Notes on design alternatives where a claim element corresponds to a feature your engineering team may be able to change. These notes will be written in engineering terms, not claim language. Richard Henderson.
Partner review of each chart before it is sent to you. Heather Munoz.
Continued status checks on the watch list. Kelly Snyder.

blocks.text: 4. Budget
The engagement budget is {{fact:f:E-2020-001.fee}}. Time recorded to date is within the portion of the budget planned for screening and the first charts, and we do not expect to ask for a change.
The items in section 5 are the ones that could alter that. If any of them begins to affect cost, we will raise it with you before the time is spent.
5. Risks
Each risk is listed with what is being done about it.

items: Pending applications. A pending application can issue with claims broader than those published. The watch list reduces this risk but cannot remove it. The memorandum will state the date as of which it speaks.

Design changes. The charts are read against the product description your team confirmed. A change to a charted feature means that chart must be read again. Please tell us of a proposed change as soon as it is under consideration.
File history length. Some short-listed patents have long prosecution records. Kelly Snyder has flagged their review as the largest open item in the time estimate. We will report if it moves.
Claim terms. Some claim terms have no settled meaning. Where a term could be read more than one way, the memorandum will say so and give a view under each reading.
Related filings. A short-listed family may have a continuation still pending, which can issue with new claims. Any such continuation is on the watch list, and the memorandum will identify each one.

blocks.text: 6. Requests

The charts are only reliable if the product description behind them is current. Please confirm that the description approved at the working session still matches the design. Please also name an engineering contact who can answer feature questions as the remaining charts are drafted.
7. Contacts

Questions about the search or the charts can come to me. Questions about legal conclusions should go to Heather Munoz. Kelly Snyder holds the watch list and the file histories, and can answer questions on either.

blocks.text: Result

Claim charts are complete for most of the short list. On the charts reviewed, most patents appear unlikely to stand in the way of the current design, subject to the qualifications the memorandum will carry.
Two questions remain open before drafting can start: validity of one patent family, and whether one product feature can be changed.
Points Discussed

Claim charts. Richard Henderson took the meeting through the charts finished since the last session. For most patents, at least one element of each independent claim has no counterpart in the product as described.
The charts still open cover the families ranked last. Richard Henderson expects no change of approach for them.
Heather Munoz noted that the internal risk ranking is a working tool. It will not appear in the memorandum in that form.

Validity question. Kelly Snyder reported on the file history of the family held for separate review. The applicant narrowed the claims during prosecution to obtain allowance, and that narrowing may limit how far the claims can now be read.
Richard Henderson has located prior art that bears on validity, and his review is under way. Heather Munoz said the memorandum will treat this family on its own and will not rest on invalidity alone.

Design alternatives. One claim element corresponds to a feature that may be changeable. Barbara Blair will ask the engineering team whether the feature can be modified, and what a change would cost in time.
Richard Henderson will send a note describing that claim element in engineering terms. The engineering team should not need to read the claim to answer.
Watch list. Kelly Snyder reported that no application on the watch list has issued since the last session. Docket checks continue.

Memorandum. Barbara Blair asked for a summary she can take to her leadership at {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}}. Heather Munoz agreed to put a short summary at the front of the memorandum, with the same qualifications and the same privilege marking as the body.
Heather Munoz asked that the summary not be circulated apart from the memorandum. Barbara Blair agreed.
Barbara Blair asked when the draft would be ready. Heather Munoz said drafting starts when both open questions are answered. She will propose a delivery date at that point.
Time and cost. Kelly Snyder reported that time recorded remains within the estimate. The validity review is the largest item still to come, and she will flag it if it runs long.
Actions Agreed

items: Richard Henderson: send the engineering note on the claim element at issue.
Richard Henderson: finish the remaining claim charts and the validity review.
Barbara Blair: return the engineering team's answer on the feature change.
Kelly Snyder: keep docket checks on the watch list current and report any issuance at once.
Heather Munoz: review the remaining charts, then begin the draft memorandum when the validity review and the engineering answer are in.

blocks.text: A further session will be called only if the engineering answer changes the analysis.
Freedom-to-Operate Analysis: Status Report
Privileged and Confidential: Attorney-Client Communication
Client: {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}}. Prepared by Richard Henderson, Patent Agent. Team: Heather Munoz, Partner; Kelly Snyder, Associate.
Summary

The analysis is substantively complete. The draft memorandum is written and is with Heather Munoz for final review. What remains is her review, delivery of the signed memorandum, and a closing call to go through the conclusions.
The memorandum states a view on each patent on the short list, with the reasons for it. Each view is qualified. None should be repeated outside the memorandum without its qualifications.
Progress Since the Last Report

rows: Every short-listed patent is now charted against the confirmed product description.
Prior art was reviewed for the family held for separate treatment at the last working session. The findings are in the draft memorandum.
The engineering note went to your team. Their answer on the feature change is reflected in the draft.
Kelly Snyder's review of the prosecution records is built into each chart.
The status of each pending application was rechecked and the docket updated.

blocks.text: Contents of the Memorandum
The draft is arranged in the following order.

items: A short summary at the front, carrying the same qualifications and privilege marking as the body.
The product description relied on, as confirmed by your team.
The search and screening method, and the scope of the search.
A view on each short-listed patent, grouped by family, with the claim charts attached.
Separate treatment of the family held for validity review, setting out the non-infringement and validity positions on their own terms.
The design alternative discussed with your engineering team, and their answer.
The watch list of pending applications, including pending continuations in short-listed families.
The qualifications that apply to every view in the memorandum.

blocks.text: Remaining Steps

items: Incorporate Heather Munoz's review comments into the draft. Richard Henderson.
Sign and deliver the final memorandum, marked privileged. Heather Munoz.
Hold a closing call to take you through each conclusion and the qualifications attached to it. Heather Munoz and Richard Henderson. We suggest that those who will act on the conclusions attend.
Hand over the watch list, with the status of each pending application as of delivery. Kelly Snyder.

blocks.text: Budget
The work described in this report has been done within the engagement budget of {{fact:f:E-2020-001.fee}}. The remaining steps are covered by it.
The file histories and the validity review took the most time in this period, as the last report expected. Both stayed within the estimate.
Monitoring the watch list after delivery is not part of the current engagement. If you want it continued, that is a separate discussion. Nothing will be docketed for it without your instruction.
Limits of the Analysis
These limits will also appear in the memorandum. They are set out here so that they are read first.

items: Date. The memorandum speaks as of its date. A patent that issues afterwards, including one from the watch list, is not covered.
Product description. The conclusions rest on the product description your team confirmed. A change to a charted feature should come back to us before the changed product is released.
Claim terms. Where a claim term could reasonably be read more than one way, the memorandum gives a view under each reading. A court is not bound by either.

Privilege. The memorandum is a privileged communication. Within {{fact:f:E-2020-001.client}} it should go only to those who need it to make decisions. Sharing it with anyone outside may waive privilege.

blocks.text: Before the Closing Call

The conclusions are tied to the design as your engineering team last described it. Please confirm that no charted feature has changed since their answer on the feature change. If one has, the affected chart will be read again before the memorandum is signed.
Please also send the names of those who will attend the closing call, so that the invitation and the memorandum go only to them.
Contacts
Questions about the charts or the prior art can come to me. Questions about the conclusions should go to Heather Munoz. Kelly Snyder holds the watch list until it is handed over.
